rationale: The January 2024 take-private closed through a Blue Wolf-controlled purchaser with Stonepeak providing preferred equity. The June 2026 sale of LOGISTEC's Marine Terminal Division to Enstructure remains signed but unclosed, so both current owners remain active and the exit stays visibly pending.

supports: Blue Wolf controls the purchaser and Stonepeak invested through preferred equity

evidence.purpose: Direct buyer evidence for the signed Marine Terminal Division acquisition
supports: The agreement covers LOGISTEC's marine terminal operations
The transaction was announced but not shown as legally closed by the cutoff

evidence.purpose: Regulatory evidence identifying the pending transaction parties
supports: Regulatory clearance does not by itself establish legal closing

companyFieldUpdates.subsector: Marine cargo handling, terminal operations and port services
companyFieldUpdates.description: LOGISTEC operates marine cargo-handling terminals and port-services infrastructure across Canada and the United States. The Marine Terminal Division serves industrial shippers, port users and public-sector counterparties through a network of North American facilities. Blue Wolf Capital Partners has controlled the platform since the January 8, 2024 take-private, with Stonepeak participating as a preferred-equity investor. Enstructure's acquisition of the Marine Terminal Division was announced on June 15, 2026 but had not legally closed by the verification cutoff; CoreAqua and SANEXEN are outside this PortCo perimeter.
